CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.

Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

1. Region is Seluma Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Government of Seluma Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Seluma. 4. Regional House of Representatives, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is the Regional House of Representatives of Seluma Regency. 5. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Seluma Regency. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of the Regional Government of Seluma Regency. 7. Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

REGENT OF SELUMA

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

CHAPTER XI

Article 24

1. Officials appointed to implement integrated protection, services and recovery who do not carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to actions and or sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations;
2. P2TP2A managers who in carrying out the duties of protection, services and recovery of victims of violence, violate the principles of implementation of protection, services and 15 recovery may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the internal mechanisms of P2TP2A and sanctions in accordance with the provisions of applicable Laws and Regulations.

Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Article 1

Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. CHAPTER I

Article 1

Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

Child is a person who has not yet reached 18 years of age, including those in the womb. 8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence and/or threats of violence that include physical, sexual, psychological, economic and/or social violence, in the family, community and/or society, in conflict situations, post-conflict, and the state. 9. Implementation is all actions that include Protection, Services, and Recovery for victims of violence. 10. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

I. GENERAL

Various acts of violence both against women and children within the household and outside the household continue to increase from time to time. This condition, if without serious handling, will destroy the life of households, society, nation and state. Therefore, the government of Seluma Regency is obliged to provide protection to women and children victims of violence which is an implementation of various laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Crime of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

On that basis, the government of Seluma Regency has taken steps as an effort to provide protection to women and children victims of violence, but has not been able to provide maximum and adequate protection against acts of violence that occur in the social life of the community, especially to women and children, among others caused by the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a regulation in the form of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is needed to answer while providing legal certainty in the protection of women and children victims from acts of violence that occur.

The existence of a Regional Regulation concerning Implementation of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government starting from prevention of acts of violence to handling of victims of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the government, Regional Government and community participation of the business sector and the community, it is hoped that violence against women and children can be reduced and even in time will be eliminated from this beloved Seluma Regency.

Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the regional government, family, advocates/paralegals, social institutions, the community, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties. 11. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children in minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children who are victims of conflict who experience physical violence or trauma, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect. 12. Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of violence to be more empowered, both physically, psychologically, socially, economically, culturally and politically. 13. Organizer is a government institution as well as social institutions, religious institutions, customary institutions, in accordance with their respective duties and functions, including providing the necessary facilities for victim recovery. 14. Violence is any act and/or threat of act that results in or may result in suffering or distress whether physical, psychological, sexual or neglect. 15. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or distress to women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or distress physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 17. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or bodily disability to a person, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 18. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person. 19. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 20. Sexual Harassment is any sexual action/behavior/gesture that is unwanted in verbal (words) or written form, physical, non-verbal, and visual for sexual purposes, having sexual content, thus causing anger, feelings of humiliation, shame, discomfort, and insecurity for others. 21. Domestic neglect is the act of neglecting women and/or children within the scope of the household who according to the applicable law for the person concerned or due to agreement or contract he/she is obliged to provide life, care, or maintenance for that person. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. 22. Service is an action that must be immediately taken for victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 23. Assistance is all actions carried out in the form of complaint services, health, advocacy and legal aid, social rehabilitation including spiritual guidance, counseling, psychological therapy and economic empowerment, repatriation and social reintegration for the purpose of strengthening and advocacy as well as recovery of victims of violence. 24. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to assist victims in conducting counseling, therapy and advocacy for the purpose of strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence. 25. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychological, and legal services involving health workers, education workers, social institutions, law enforcement officers, psychologists, psychiatrists, volunteer assistants and/or spiritual counselors. 26. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an institution for victim recovery from health, education and economic independence aspects. 27. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards. 28.
